ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input u(t) enters the first summing point from the left as a positive input; the output node of the first integrator is denoted as x1(t), and this node on one hand is fed back through gain 3 to the negative terminal of the first summing point, and on the other hand is sent through gain 2 to the positive terminal of the second summing point; the output y(t) is taken from the output terminal of the second integrator, and is respectively fed back through gain 9 to the negative terminal of the first summing point and through gain 12 to the negative terminal of the second summing point. Reasoning: Let X1(s) be the output of the first integrator, and Y(s) be the output of the second integrator. From the input relation of the first integrator, sX1 = U - 3X1 - 9Y, that is, (s+3)X1 + 9Y = U. From the input relation of the second integrator, sY = 2X1 - 12Y, that is, (s+12)Y = 2X1. From the second equation, X1 = (s+12)Y/2. Substitute into the first equation: ((s+3)(s+12)/2 + 9)Y = U, so Y/U = 2/((s+3)(s+12)+18) = 2/(s^2+15s+54) = 2/((s+6)(s+9)). Writing it in standard first-order factor form: 2/((s+6)(s+9)) = 1/[27(1+s/6)(1+s/9)].

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram connections: the first integrator has local negative feedback via gain 3, the second integrator has local negative feedback via gain 12, and the output y is also fed back through gain 9 to the first summing junction. Collapse the first local loop: from the first summer's net external input e = u - 9y to the first integrator output, the equivalent transfer is (1/s)/(1+3/s)=1/(s+3). Collapse the second local loop: from the signal after gain 2 to y, the equivalent transfer is (1/s)/(1+12/s)=1/(s+12). Include the gain 2 between the two loops, giving the forward transfer from e to y as F(s)=2/[(s+3)(s+12)]. Finally close the remaining negative feedback through gain 9: G(s)=F/(1+9F)=2/[s^2+15s+54]=2/[(s+6)(s+9)]=1/[27(1+s/6)(1+s/9)].
